description: One unit of thought in a vault: something you wrote, a passage you kept, a link, a file, a piece of code, or a post. Kept as a Markdown file in the vault's folder and never written to a PDS; publishing makes a com.ohmmmm.post from it. The folder a block's file is in is its home channel. The file's name is its slug.

kind.description: What the block is. Read from the content when not given: one fenced code block is code, one embedded file is file or media, one address is link, otherwise text. A post file (see visibility) is a post. Treat a kind you do not know as text.

body.description: Markdown as Obsidian reads it: CommonMark with footnotes, fenced code in any language, [[slug]] and [[slug|words]] links, ![[file]] embeds, @handle mentions and #tags.

channels.description: Channels the block is in besides its home channel, each as a channel's path in the vault, such as writing/collisions.

origin.description: Where the original lives when it is not this file: a local path (absolute or starting ~/), a Google Drive path (gdrive:My Drive/...) or the Drive folder's mounted path, an HTTP(S) address, or an AT URI. Size, time and hash of the original are kept in the vault's index, not here.

from.description: The ID of the source this block was captured from.

by.description: Who made the block: me, or agent:<name>. An agent's block starts private until the member moves it.

visibility.description: Which layer the block is kept in, and so who can read it. public: published on the PDS, readable by anyone. friends: kept readable by the vault service and shown to the friends the member chose. private: encrypted, with keys only on the member's devices. A block that does not say is private. A file with visibility, no kind, and none of origin, from, excerpt, by, status, created or updated is read as a post file.

excerpt.description: The exact words kept from a source, with the text around them, so the passage can be found again when the source's text is captured anew.

position.description: Where the quote starts in the source's text, in characters.
